newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak VSZ losses pull SAX index down further.
newsitem.headline: Slovak VSZ losses pull SAX index down further.

text.p: Major Slovak shares continued their freefall in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with losses to shares of VSZ steel pulling the SAX index down.

The index, which eased 5.04 points to 161.82, has now lost over 25 percent since it began its downturn at the end of August. And brokers said they remained pessimistic, expecting further losses in near future.
"I think it will decline yet for a while, but then, maybe soon, investor interest could strengthen as the share prices become significantly low," Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said.

Steel maker VSZ, currently the most liquid blue chip, closed down 18 crowns at 467, but lost 15.41 percent in the average price, while oil refinery Slovnaft closed up 20 crowns at 710, but traded only eight shares.
"Now we can see the real price of VSZ, as a package of some 5,000 shares, which had artificially kept its value over several past weeks, finaly disappeared," Briska said.
The country's largest commercial bank, VUB, edged down 30 crowns to 1,670.
Overall volume increased to 237,789 shares, from 64,853 shares traded on Wednesday, while turnover rose to 185.26 million crowns, from 42.744 million.
